_mechanism: Compound-heterozygous BUBR1 hypomorph (one truncating + one kinase-domain missense allele): residual BUBR1 is low; goal is to raise/stabilise it and never weaken the SAC further.

SIRT2.why: deacetylates BUBR1 K668, protecting it from degradation

NAMPT.why: rate-limiting NAD+ salvage enzyme feeding SIRT2

CREBBP.why: acetylates BUBR1 K668 (promotes its loss); activators are harmful
CREBBP.no_propose_why: CREBBP/EP300 loss causes Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome and both are tumour suppressors; used only to exclude activators

EP300.no_propose_why: CREBBP/EP300 loss causes Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome and both are tumour suppressors; used only to exclude activators

curated_candidates.mechanism: Raises NAD+ -> SIRT2 deacetylation of BUBR1 K668 -> less degradation
refs: North BJ et al., EMBO J 2014 (SIRT2/NMN raise BubR1 in mice)
NR open-label studies in ataxia-telangiectasia incl. children (VERIFY citation)

curated_candidates.mechanism: Approved medicine; raises blood NAD+ up to 8-fold in humans -> SIRT2 -> BUBR1 K668 deacetylation
refs: Pirinen E et al. Cell Metab 2020;31(6):1078-90 (niacin raised blood NAD+ in humans)
North BJ et al. EMBO J 2014 (NAD+ -> SIRT2 -> BubR1)

curated_candidates.mechanism: Same axis as NR; directly tested in BubR1 mice
refs: North BJ et al., EMBO J 2014

curated_candidates.direction: up at low dose; sirtuin-inhibitory at high conc. (CAUTION)

curated_candidates.mechanism: Low-BubR1 cells more sensitive to oxidative stress
Clears senescent cells; reserve only (cytotoxic kinase inhibitor)
refs: Baker DJ et al., Nature 2011 (p16 senescent-cell clearance in BubR1 hypomorphs)

lincs._about: Signature-reversal settings. Alarm genes = p53/apoptosis/interferon genes; drugs that switch them off are flagged (they would let aneuploid cells survive). Top-level exclude_patterns and known_mechanisms also apply.

known_mechanisms._about: Curated mechanisms for research compounds that DGIdb/Open Targets do not annotate (from vendor/literature descriptions); used only to EXCLUDE wrong-direction agents.
